HARDY_58.text: G. H. Hardy, A Course of Pure Mathematics, 3rd ed. (1921), Sec. 58 'Definition of a limit': phi(n) tends to l if for every eps > 0 there is n0(eps) with |phi(n) - l| < eps for all n >= n0.

HARDY_60.text: Hardy, A Course of Pure Mathematics, Sec. 60, Definition II: phi(n) tends to +inf if for every Delta there is n0(Delta) with phi(n) > Delta for ALL n >= n0; likewise -inf.

HARDY_62.text: Hardy, A Course of Pure Mathematics, Sec. 62 'Oscillating functions': when phi(n) does not tend to a limit, nor to +inf, nor to -inf, phi(n) oscillates; finitely if bounded, infinitely otherwise. Examples in the text: (-1)^n, (-1)^n + 1/n, (-1)^n n; a continual repetition of a cycle of values certainly oscillates. Examples XXIV.7: sin(n theta pi) oscillates finitely for irrational theta.
HARDY_62.status: VERIFIED: Project Gutenberg #38769 text, Sec. 62 and Examples XXIV.7

HARDY_72.text: Hardy, A Course of Pure Mathematics, Sec. 72 'The limit of x^n': x^n -> +inf (x > 1), -> 0 (-1 < x < 1), oscillates finitely (x = -1), oscillates infinitely (x < -1).

HARDY_77.text: Hardy, A Course of Pure Mathematics, Sec. 77, the remark following theorem (7): the converse of (7) fails, since 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + ... diverges to +inf although 1/n -> 0.
HARDY_77.status: VERIFIED: Project Gutenberg #38769 text, Sec. 77, remark after (7)

HARDY_188.text: Hardy, A Course of Pure Mathematics, Sec. 188 'Alternating series': if phi(n) decreases steadily to 0, phi(0) - phi(1) + phi(2) - ... converges and its sum lies between phi(0) and phi(0) - phi(1). Applied to the tail after the k-th term this gives |S - S_k| <= a_{k+1}.
HARDY_188.status: VERIFIED: Project Gutenberg #38769 text, Sec. 188 (the tail bound is the theorem applied to the tail)

ALT_SERIES_EST.text: Alternating series estimation theorem: |S_k - L| <= a_{k+1}. Wikipedia, 'Alternating series test', section 'Alternating series estimation theorem'.
ALT_SERIES_EST.status: VERIFIED: en.wikipedia.org raw page fetched 2026-10-14 (secondary source)

RUDIN_3_1.text: W. Rudin, Principles of Mathematical Analysis, 3rd ed. (McGraw-Hill, 1976), Definition 3.1, p. 47: a sequence {p_n} in a metric space X converges if there is a point p in X such that for every eps > 0 there is an integer N with d(p_n, p) < eps for all n >= N.

RW_RECURRENT.text: A simple random walk on Z crosses every point infinitely often (recurrence; Polya 1921). Wikipedia, 'Random walk', one-dimensional section.
RW_RECURRENT.status: VERIFIED: en.wikipedia.org raw page fetched 2026-10-14 (secondary source)

BOREL_CANTELLI.text: Second Borel-Cantelli lemma: independent events with divergent probability sum occur infinitely often with probability 1 (Wikipedia, 'Borel-Cantelli lemma', citing Feller and Durrett). So a non-degenerate iid sequence a.s. has |x_{n+1} - x_n| > delta infinitely often for some delta > 0 and does not converge.
BOREL_CANTELLI.status: VERIFIED: en.wikipedia.org raw page fetched 2026-10-14 (secondary source)

NIST_6442.text: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Sec. 6.4.4.2 'Stationarity': mean, variance and autocorrelation structure do not change over time: no trend, constant variance, constant autocorrelation and no periodic fluctuations (seasonality).

SHNOL_2007.text: E. Shnol, 'Stability of equilibria', Scholarpedia 2(3):2770 (2007): Lyapunov stability takes into account only perturbations of the initial conditions.

KERAS_ES.text: Keras EarlyStopping / MonitorCallback: 'min_delta: Minimum change in the monitored quantity to qualify as an improvement, i.e. an absolute change of less than min_delta, will count as no improvement'; _is_improvement(monitor, reference) = monitor_op(monitor - min_delta, reference), with min_delta negated for mode 'min' (monitor_op = less): an improvement is current < best - min_delta.

HARDY_XXIV5.text: Hardy, A Course of Pure Mathematics, Examples XXIV.5: n^2 + (-1)^n 2n -> +inf, progressing 'by a continual series of steps forwards and backwards'; it does not oscillate according to the definition of Sec. 62.
HARDY_XXIV5.status: VERIFIED: Project Gutenberg #38769 text, Examples XXIV.5

STATIONARY_WIKI.text: Wikipedia, 'Stationary process', section 'Weak or wide-sense stationarity', Eq. 3 (citing Park 2018, p. 159): a WSS process has a constant mean function m_X(t) = E[X_t], an autocovariance K_XX(t1, t2) that depends only on the difference t1 - t2, and a finite second moment E|X_t|^2 for all t. (At t1 = t2 the variance K_XX(t, t) is then constant. What this corpus derives from it about deterministic sequences is OUR derivation, stated in the equilibrium definition, not the page's.)
STATIONARY_WIKI.status: VERIFIED: en.wikipedia.org raw page (action=raw) fetched 2026-10-14 (secondary source): Eq. 3 and the two sentences after it; the parenthesis is OUR reading of the second condition at zero lag

SETTLING_WIKI.text: Wikipedia, 'Settling time' (control theory): the time for the output to enter 'and remain within a specified error band'; quoting Tay, Mareels and Moore, High Performance Control (1998), p. 93: 'the time required for the response curve to reach and stay within a range of certain percentage (usually 5% or 2%) of the final value'.

PYCONTROL_STEPINFO.text: python-control, control.step_info: 'SettlingTime: Time to enter inside a default error of 2%'; SettlingTimeThreshold 'Defines the error to compute settling time (default = 0.02)'.

HARDY_69.text: Hardy, A Course of Pure Mathematics, Sec. 69: if phi(n) increases steadily with n, then either phi(n) tends to a limit or phi(n) -> +inf (and likewise for a steadily decreasing phi).

HARDY_73.text: Hardy, A Course of Pure Mathematics, Sec. 73: {1 + 1/n}^n increases steadily and stays below 3, so it tends to a limit, denoted e; Sec. 208 identifies it with the number e.

IEEE754.text: IEEE Std 754-2008: under roundTiesToEven an overflow goes to +-inf with the sign of the intermediate result (7.4 a); multiplication(0, inf) and multiplication(inf, 0) are invalid operations whose default result is a quiet NaN (7.2 b); an operation with quiet NaN inputs delivers a quiet NaN (6.2). The 2019 revision was not checked.

definitions.question: Does the sequence tend to a finite limit?
definitions.rule: REPORTED, NOT SCORED: true iff props.limit is a number. A whole-sequence property that no windowed observer can decide at checkpoint n. The observer's `converged` is an online verdict at n, scored against the CONVENTION question alone; scoring one reading against both questions contradicts itself wherever a sequence converges but has not settled yet (or settles without converging), so even a perfect observer would fail.

definitions.question: From checkpoint n on, does the sequence stay within eps of a point?
definitions.rule: eps(L) = 1e-3*max(|L|, 1e-3) (the observer's dh_zero and scale). With a limit L: |x_m - L| <= eps(L) for every m in [n, H]. Without a limit and bounded: the tail x_n..x_H fits in a ball of radius eps(centre). Unbounded or tending to +-inf: false. H = max(20000, 10n) generated values: a horizon, not a proof.

definitions.question: Does the sequence tend to +inf or -inf?
definitions.rule: true iff props.tends_to is '+inf' or '-inf'. Whole-sequence.

definitions.question: Does it tend neither to a limit nor to +inf nor to -inf (Hardy Sec. 62)?
definitions.rule: true iff props.limit is null and props.tends_to is null. Whole-sequence: a transient oscillation of a convergent sequence does not count, and a run to +inf by steps forwards and backwards does not oscillate (Examples XXIV.5).

definitions.question: Is the sequence weakly stationary (NIST 6.4.4.2): a constant mean AND a constant variance, an autocovariance that depends only on the lag, and no periodic fluctuation?
definitions.rule: Standard, under the owner's delegation for inherited names (#1754 comment 6178341982). A deterministic row: true iff certify.py certifies it constant. OUR derivation from the cited definition (the one modelling choice recorded on #1754): a deterministic sequence is the degenerate process X_t = x_t, whose mean function is x_t (and whose variance is 0), so it is weakly stationary iff it is constant. This is not a claim about random-phase processes such as Wikipedia's Example 2, X_t = cos(t + Y) with a random Y, which is stationary because Y is random. A random-process row: false if any of props.has_trend, props.periodic, props.variance_changes is true (NIST 6.4.4.2), true if all three are false; the flags follow from the process kind (iid noise: stationary; a random walk x_0 + n steps has the constant mean x_0 but the variance n sigma^2, so it is NOT in equilibrium).

definitions.question: Did the value set a new best (lower is better) within the last 10 steps, and is the sequence eventually bounded?
definitions.rule: Owner ruling (#1754, corrected): a new best (lower) by more than min_delta within the window, AND the sequence is EVENTUALLY bounded (props.bounded: lim sup |x_n| < inf, #1758 comment 6173870348; Hardy Sec. 62: it neither diverges nor oscillates infinitely). The new-best part is Keras EarlyStopping mode='min', epoch by epoch, with ONE deliberate deviation: Keras starts best=inf so epoch 0 is always an improvement; here best starts at x_0 and x_0 is a baseline, never an improvement (a value cannot improve on nothing); x_i is an improvement iff x_i < best - min_delta, and then best = x_i. improving@n iff an improvement occurred at some i in [max(1, n-9), n] (patience = the 10-step window). min_delta = 1e-3*max(|best|, 1e-3) is OUR documented choice (the observer's rtol and scale); it is not PyTorch's rel threshold, which is best*(1 - threshold) and differs when best < 0.

definitions.question: From checkpoint n on, does the value stay within a band about where it is heading?
definitions.rule: Owner decision (#1754): settled within a band, control theory's settling criterion ('reach and stay within a range of certain percentage (usually 5% or 2%) of the final value'). Same shape as CONVENTION converged with the band beta(L) = 1e-2*max(|L|, 1e-3) in place of eps: OUR documented choice, the observer's coarse dh_small tier, not a value from the cited texts. With a limit L: |x_m - L| <= beta(L) for every m in [n, H]. Bounded without a limit: the tail x_n..x_H fits a ball of radius beta(centre). Unbounded or tending to +-inf: false. Since beta >= eps, CONVENTION converged implies CONVENTION stable; derive.py asserts it at every checkpoint.

definitions.question: At a checkpoint whose current value x_n is NaN: what does each predicate answer?
definitions.rule: The #1758 O2 convention (#1746: NaN is undefined): while the current value is NaN every predicate is false, whatever the whole sequence does. It is not a MATH answer (Hardy Sec. 62 would call an absorbing NaN tail neither convergent nor tending to +-inf, so oscillating), so every predicate at such a checkpoint is labelled CONVENTION with this citation, before or after the row's regime (x_n alone decides it): the one recorded exception to one question per predicate.
